attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'No closer to a solution' fairly becomes no progress toward solving alignment from about April 2022 to mid-2024. It is a firm, unhedged retrospective observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. It separates progress on subproblems from progress toward a general solution, but Marcus gave no measure of distance to a solution, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Constitutional AI (Dec 2022, inside the period) reports more precise behavioural control. That is local control of current models and does not show the general barrier was reduced.
Weak-to-strong paper (Dec 2023) works on a key supervision obstacle, but only through an analogy. The authors say naive methods fall short. This is potential counterevidence, not shown to transfer.
International interim report (May 2024): some recent systems are more controllable, but whether future systems will be is unclear. This does not settle distance to a solution.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows real alignment research advances in the period (e1, e2), which weighs against a literal 'no progress'. But under the contract, none is shown to reduce a substantive barrier to a general solution, and e3 calls future controllability unclear. There is no comparable 2022 vs 2024 baseline, so the evidence settles neither the support nor the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the investment backdrop and the persistence of unreliability, toxicity and hallucinations. It does not claim there were no improvements.

contract.note: Limiting scope to contemporary LLMs and asking whether the failures persist, rather than whether every case fails, is a fair, ordinary reading. The Jan–Jun 2024 window is the evaluator's choice but a reasonable one.

evidence.note: UK AISI evaluation (May 2024): models hallucinated constraints and task completion, finished no long-horizon tasks, and safeguards were easily bypassed.
April 2024 benchmark: tested open models still mishandle toxicity or hallucinate, though results differ by model.
Stanford AI Index: generative AI investment was about $3B in 2022 and $25B in 2023. This confirms the tens-of-billions backdrop.

reviews.rationale: Independent evaluations from inside the 2024 window document hallucinations, unreliable task execution and toxicity/safeguard failures in prominent LLMs. Stanford data confirms tens of billions in investment since 2022. Strong results on some tasks do not meet the contradiction condition.
